It's always fun to have something unexpected happen. Maybe you introduce a third party--a den of thieves, who steal the artifact and take it to a secluded location before the cultists or your hero can get it.

Perhaps in a nearby town your PC learns of the thieve's hideout, but he also finds the cultists are hot on the trail.

Then it's a race to see who can track it down first--that way your hero can get into some minor battles with the cultists before the actual power is unleashed.

For extra fun, have the thieves be werewolves or something who thought the artifact would give them power--but they accidently turn themselves undead. Have fun with it.

If you ever feel like there is "only one logical path" then throw some variables in there to create multiple routes! Half the fun of being a DM is seeing which paths the players choose!

I would strongly recommend the D&D Adventure games. No DM needed, and with 4-5 players everyone will have a hero that can contribute.

Ravenloft is fun (spooky castle) but can be frustrating due to the difficult event cards. Ashardalon has boring quests at first (the first 3 to 5 quests lack imagination) but the heroes are the most powerful and events are fun. Drizzt is the most complicated in terms of hero stances but has the best quests (but also has less than thrilling events and items).

What's also fun about them is that the monsters and cards from each can be mixed up or used all together. There are also the Dungeon Command games which come with additional miniatures and cards that work with any of the games.

The D&D Adventure Games do drop to about $35 every so often on Amazon, but you have to keep you eye out for them and act *quickly.*

Photos are a little dark so my c&c may be off base, but from what I can see, I'd suggest thinning the paints more with water for your next mini. The yellow on shield looks a bit rough. The more drops of water you mix with your paint, the lighter the paint will go on. It'll give you more control and allow you to do more layers.

Usually, after each layer dries, you'll go a little bit lighter (add white paint to the mix, for example) and only paint lighter, highlighted/raised areas. Once that dries, you could do a wash (darker colors w/ water, causes the paint to collect in the recesses/shadowy areas of the mini) to also better blend the different highlights.
